classes.name: Oral corticosteroids
classes.description: Systemic oral corticosteroids: prednisone (tablets, solution; Rayos delayed-release appears discontinued), methylprednisolone (Medrol, dose pack), prednisolone (solution, Orapred ODT, Millipred), dexamethasone (tablets, solution, Dexamethasone Intensol, TaperDex/Dxevo/HiDex packs; Hemady 20 mg is labeled for multiple myeloma only, an alternative, never the pick), hydrocortisone (Cortef; Alkindi Sprinkle and Khindivi oral solution for children). Deflazacort (Emflaza) and vamorolone (Agamree) for Duchenne are specialty alternatives only, never the pick. Not budesonide (Entocort, Uceris, Tarpeyo) or inhaled/topical steroids.
classes.plainDescription: Short courses of steroid pills that calm inflammation fast, for flares of asthma, COPD, arthritis, allergies and more.
classes.indication: Inflammatory flares, asthma/COPD exacerbations, autoimmune disease, adrenal insufficiency

records.verificationNote: Read PDF p.35 (Hormonal Agents - Adrenal rows; text layer flags). Prednisone tablet and therapy pack, prednisone and prednisolone solutions, dexamethasone, methylprednisolone and hydrocortisone are Tier 1 with no flags. Medrol 2 mg brand is Tier 2 and is shown as an alternative; the generic methylprednisolone is Tier 1, so this is not a brand-over-generic BOGL. The list prints no strength or course for prednisone; 10 mg tablet is the brief's strength. Named brand-only products absent from the document are recorded nonformulary under the closed-list statement (PDF p.2). [Sonnet check 2026-11-20: removed 1 brand-name entries (TaperDex) whose generic is listed; PDF p.3 says only that the brand is 'generally considered non-formulary and subject to a higher cost share' when a generic is available, which is a hedge, not an exclusion, so no barrier is recorded. Where a brand's own generic form is absent from the list the entry stays.]

records.verificationNote: Read from the formulary text layer, row by row (each tier digit sits on the same row as its drug name; pypdf gave no x-coordinates for the digits). Formulary sig and quantity limits are as printed; the document prints no sig, so the sig is the label starting dose. Prednisone 10 mg tablet is Tier 1 with no PA; BvsD is a Part B versus Part D review flag, not a PA, so it is not in preferredRestriction (PDG p. 61). Not listed: Rayos, Medrol, Orapred ODT, Millipred, Cortef, TaperDex, Dxevo, HiDex. Hydrocortisone tablets print on p. 54 (in the list's dermatology block) and are cited as printed.
